name: Town hall on the skate park
description: Residents debate whether the town should build a skate park. A moderator chairs: residents raise hands, speak when recognized, move and second a motion, amend it, and the moderator calls the question. The meeting ends with the vote on the main motion.

debate.description: Speeches the coded chair waits for before calling the question.

brief.situation: Riverside's town council holds a public meeting on one question: should the town build a skate park? Parents want a safe place for kids; neighbours worry about noise and cost.
brief.rules: The moderator chairs. Raise your hand to ask for the floor and speak only when recognized (at most two speeches each time). Any resident may move a motion once recognized; a motion needs a second before it is debated. The open motion can be amended once seconded, and the amendment is voted on first. When the moderator calls the question, every resident votes yes, no or abstain; the motion passes with more than half of the votes cast, and the meeting ends.

roles.resident: You are a resident. {$'You want the park built.' if $actor.stance > 0.3 else ($'You are open to a compromise.' if $actor.stance > -0.3 else 'You are against the park.')} Argue for what you want and vote for it.
roles.moderator: You chair the meeting. Give the floor fairly, keep debate moving, and call the question once the motion before the body has been debated.

hall.question: Should Riverside build a skate park?

supermajority.description: Two thirds of the votes cast are needed.

my_view.show: Your leaning: {$'for the park' if $actor.stance > 0.3 else ($'undecided, open to a compromise' if $actor.stance > -0.3 else 'against the park')}.

with.text: Riverside builds a skate park by the river by June.
